spans.s:
Dhruva
(‘the steady one’)
------------------------------------------
Along with प्रह्लाद, ध्रुव too has carved out for himself a permanent place in the annals of child-devotees in our पुराणस्.
Dhruva was the elder son of the king Uttānapāda from his first wife Sunīti. Enamoured of Suruci, his second wife, the king had completely neglected Sunīti and her son ध्रुव.
Once, snubbed by his step-मोथेर् Suruci in the presence of his ड़थेर्, ध्रुव became despondent and approached his मोथेर् for solace. She advised him to pray to Lord विष्णु by performing austerities.
When he was going to the forest, the sage नारद met him and instructed him in meditation. After a severe penance, ध्रुव had a vision of Lord विष्णु who gave him the boon of the kingdom. He also bestowed on him a long, happy life here and a permanent abode in the heavenly regions after death. That is now known as ‘Dhruvanakṣatra’ (pole-star).
Once, Uttama, younger brother of ध्रुव, went to the हिमालयस् on a hunting expedition but was killed in an encounter with the yakṣas (a kind of demigods) who were the followers of कुबेर. Enraged by this, ध्रुव attacked them, killing them in large numbers. कुबेर was forced to fight with ध्रुव when Svāyambhuva मनु (the forefather of ध्रुव) appeared on the scene and stopped the fight. Then the two became friends.
Dhruva ruled his kingdom according to the highest principles of धर्म for many years.
